content:
Construct a good set by taking \(p^2\) for every prime \(p\le 43\), since \(43^2=1849\le 2016\). There are \(14\) such primes, so this gives \(14\) pairwise coprime composites.

For the upper bound, let \(n\) be any composite in a good set, and let \(p\) be its smallest prime divisor. Then \(p\le \sqrt n \le \sqrt{2016}<45\), so \(p\le 43\). Distinct numbers in the good set must have distinct smallest prime divisors, or else they would share a common divisor. Therefore the good set has at most the number of primes \(\le 43\), which is \(14\).

\[
\boxed{14}
\]
